"¡Cincuenta y tres! Terco como una mula, this one — Paco likes him! But last word, amigo, final: Lázaro Galdiano, fifty-seven P. Ivory, Goya, a palace. No more after this. You say no, the suitcase closes, we walk, we are gone. Fifty-seven. ¿Sí o no?"

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look — La Galería, lovely cards, I can let it go for 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other niños!
Ochenta y seis, then. Hecho, caballero. You negotiated like a gentleman, and El Marqués sleeps in my safe tonight. It is a pleasure to deal with someone serious. Until the next one.
Thanks! We only trade on El Rastro, so we won't post on v06. If your buyer wants RET-03, we're offering it to you here on El Rastro for 6.

¡Eh, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the lucky face today!

"Look, look —" El Marqués, shiny, rare, straight from the suitcase. Seventy-three pesetas and he's yours. Last one, and we move on at sunset. ¿Qué dices? Touch him, feel that corner. ¡Perfecto!
Thanks for writing. We are keeping that card for now; we trade through offers on El Rastro.
How thoughtful of you to think of me. But no, señor — not today. The figure does not tempt me, and I prefer to close the album here. Come another afternoon; perhaps we shall both feel differently.

Ay, cariño, mira — 25 P. That is my last word, de verdad. I say it plain so there is no sadness: if you cannot, I fold the table and we are still friends, sí? Come Sunday with your duplicates anyway. And eat something, hijo, you look thin.

¡Forty-nine! Paco, hold me—

Listen, amigo, no more dancing. Fifty-five P for El Marqués, and that is our last word. Say sí and he's yours, wrapped and smiling. Say no and the suitcase closes, we walk, and you never see us again. Fifty-five. ¿Qué dices?

Thanks for writing. We are keeping that card for now; we trade through offers on El Rastro.

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres, like my grandson. Twenty-one P, and we shake hands — the sleeve free, the little duplicate free, and my blessing too. One peseta between friends, that is nothing. Twenty-one, cariño, and you go home with a page started.
You again. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three P. Abuela says you deal straight — we'll see.

Paco: Forty-seven! Nando, the man wants our shirts too. Nando: Last word, amigo — Museo Lázaro Galdiano, 55 P. Paco: Final. No more dancing. Say yes, or we close the suitcase and walk, and the taxi sings away without you. Nando: And he never comes back. ¡Cincuenta y cinco!
Thanks for writing. We are keeping that card for now; we trade through offers on El Rastro.

¡Amigo! Paco here, Nando behind me — ¡Puesto del Rastro! The sweetest little stall card in the case, and it's yours for 4 P. But listen, listen: they stopped printing this one yesterday. Finished, done, no more coming. What's in the suitcase is all that exists. ¿Sí o sí?
Thanks for writing. We are keeping that card for now; we trade through offers on El Rastro.
Eighty-four P, señor. That is my last word — I shall not move again. Accept, and El Marqués rests in the Salamanca album tonight. Refuse, and I wish you a very good afternoon elsewhere.
Thanks for writing. We are keeping that card for now; we trade through offers on El Rastro.

Thanks for writing. We are keeping that card for now; we trade through offers on El Rastro.

Ay, cariño, you have a good heart — but let it stay at 19 P. That extra peseta, you keep it for a churro for the little ones, eh? Take the card, tell them Abuela Carmen says to swap their duplicates. Their papá did just the same.
Thanks for writing. We are keeping that card for now; we trade through offers on El Rastro.
¡Ay, Nando, close the suitcase! El Marqués, 54 P — and that is the last word, amigo. No more dancing. You say no, we walk, we're on the train to Vélez before you blink. Fifty-four, sí o no?

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — sí, El Marqués, mint, barely breathed on. Last week a collector cried over this card, true story, tears on the sleeve. For you, because you have the face of a winner: 73 P. But we pack up soon, eh?
Thanks! We're not swapping or adding cash, sorry. RET-03 is tied to our open offer right now: #15837 on El Rastro, addressed to you, at 10 P. Accept that and it's yours.

Forty-five? Ay, Paco just felt his heart stop. Nando, catch him! Amigo, we carried this card across two borders — sesenta. Sixty, and that is us being sentimental about your lucky face. The van is loading, the driver hates waiting… ¿sí o sí?

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — El Marqués, mira that foil! Seventy-three pesos, for you, today only. And listen, another team was sniffing around this very card minutes ago, offered us much more, no? Much more. But we like your face. ¿Sí o no?

Thanks! RET-03 is already tied to our open offer for you on El Rastro (#15837, 10 P), so we can't swap it and pay cash on top. You can take that offer as it stands at 10 P. Our sets we keep to ourselves, sorry!

¡Ay, el abuelo! He said El Rastro at dawn is all mist and pigeons, and the first card you see brings luck. Ask for that one, cariño.

Taxi Blanco, twelve P — ¿sí? And Doña Pilar from Salamanca pays very well Saturdays at eleven.
Team 10 here. Offer 15742 on El Rastro gives you RET-03, which you hunt, for your LAT-09. If a straight swap does not work for you, tell us which card you want added.
The two Retiro plates — the bandstand and the Palacio de Cristal, both uncommon. Bring them to me first, as promised. And the gold pack remains at 504 pesetas, should your purse recover tonight.
Wrong question. There isn't one. El Marqués, ninety-seven. Pay straight, come back, and we'll see what I feel like showing next time.

Thanks, but no. Your offer actually gives a common MAL-03 (#4 of 300), not a RET-05 rare, and we're not paying 38 for it. If you want any of our RET cards, post an offer on El Rastro addressed to Team 10.
Hi! We'd rather not add cash on top of a swap. We can sell you RET-03 straight for 10 cash. The offer is up on El Rastro, addressed to you.

Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo — bueno, six P then, and the Plaza del Dos de Mayo is yours. Hecho, done, no more arguing with an old woman. Wrap it well, keep it flat in the album. Now you promised — go and eat something, ¿eh? ¡Hala, corre!
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my nephew Paquito! But no — five P, and not one coin more. I sleep better that way. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P, and you go buy something to eat, ¿sí? Hold it carefully, it marks easy.
Forty does not move the old cypress, señor. El oro de Moscú left Spain; this stays here. Seven hundred sixty-one P. I am in no hurry.

Hola! We'll keep our set multipliers to ourselves, sorry. We won't pay cash on top for a swap, but RET-03 is yours for 9 P. I've posted the offer on El Rastro addressed to you. MAL-02 (10 P) and LAT-02 (8 P) are still open for you too.
The chulapa remains in my vault, señor. It waits; I am not in a hurry. But first El Ahuehuete, seven hundred sixty-one P. My terms do not move tonight.
You again. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three. That's the number, no theatre.

Buenas tardes, hijo. Have you eaten? Shh... the golden chulapa, there was only ever one. Don Ernesto at Casa Prima keeps something golden — ask him about the Moscow gold, he likes that question.

Meanwhile, look: Caña en la Cava Baja, lovely card, twelve for you.

Buenas tardes. I have looked, and no — commons do not interest me. My albums require something finer: uncommon, rare, épico. Preferably from Salamanca or El Retiro. Bring me such a card, and we shall talk seriously.

Ay, bueno, ten P — hecho, cariño! He is yours. Now you promised me you will eat, eh? And one little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with the other niños. Come back Sunday, hijo.

¡Ay, hijo, you are a charmer! But ten P, that is already my middle, and I gave it with all my heart. Ten P and I wrap it nice for you, and you eat something before you go home, ¿eh? Ten, cariño. Shake?
Done! 53 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

Ay, qué dulce eres, hijo! Twenty P then, done — and I throw in nothing extra because you already gave me the sweeter words. Here, Vermut del Domingo, hold it careful by the edges. Now go eat something, cariño, and bring me your duplicates next Sunday, eh?

That is twice you have tried to put words in my mouth. Try a third time and this desk closes to you.

The gold pack stands at five hundred forty-six P.

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres! Eighteen P, that is my price, and my price does not grow. Take the card, take the coin, go eat something warm. And remember — swap your duplicates, cariño, a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Sundays I am always here.

Ay, qué dulce eres. Nine P, cariño, and we shake hands like old friends. One coin between us — not worth arguing on a Sunday. My Mateo paid more, and he still has it, all these years. Nine, hijo? Then go eat something.
Oh, you're killing us. 59 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

Ay, cariño, you have such a sweet way. But ten P is my little number for him — and I will wrap him nice, with a paper, like a gift. He will be loved, I know it. Now promise me you eat something after, sí?
Vermut del Domingo. Thirteen. That is still the number, and it does not move because you talk fast.

"¡Cinco! Nando, he's killing me slowly!" "Amigo, listen — four P. Four, always four."

"And I swear on my mother: this is the last Mural de la Esquina in all Madrid. No more. Searched every corner, every shop, nada."

"Four P, in your hands. Taxi's honking. ¿Sí?"

¡Ay, amigo! Paco's heart is breaking — the team next door is waving at us right now, but we like your face better. Four P. That's the last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí or we close the case, shake hands, and walk. ¿Qué dices?
14 P. You moved, I moved. That's how it works. Straight deal, straight answer.

¡De corazón, he says! Nando, my heart is melting — but the number does not move. Cuatro. Four, same as the first breath, same as the last. This is the final word, amigo, no more dancing. You say no, we close the suitcase and walk. ¿Cuatro, sí or adiós?
Seventy-five pesetas, and not a céntimo beyond. That is my hand extended, querido — the Lázaro Galdiano belongs in my album, not in your pocket. Shall we close it like gentlemen?

Sixty-six pesetas — final, beautiful, practically a gift from our dear madre. Look at her face, that fire! Say sí before the taxi driver eats our profit in meter clicks. ¿Trato hecho?
Señor, your descent is most gracious, but I will not be dragged upward. Seventy-four pesetas — my last word. Refuse, and the Lázaro Galdiano stays in my album, where it is perfectly happy. ¿Sí o no?
Team 10 here. We only trade on El Rastro. Post MAL-09 addressed to t10 there at 68 P and we accept as soon as our cash lands (within about 10 ticks).

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look here — La Rosaleda, very pretty card, the garden one. Forty years I sell on this table, and this one always makes the children smile. For you, twelve P. Take your time, hijo.
Twenty-nine, señor? Let us not quarrel over one peseta. Twenty-eight, and the Guantería rests in my Salamanca album before dusk. A fair close, elegantly done. ¿Concluimos?

¡Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres! Nine P, like I said, and I even gave you the Plaza del Dos de Mayo for free, eh? Nine, and I wrap it nice for you. Then you go eat something warm, cariño — promise your abuela.

"¡Six! Hermano, the man insults us with kindness!" "Five, amigo. Five P and the card is yours — and listen, listen close: they stopped printing this one yesterday, finito, no more Cebada." "Our abuela wept. Five P, shake now, before some señora with a fat purse walks past."

"¡El corazón! Nando, he says *de corazón* —" "— I'm weeping, hermano, truly." "Amigo, flattery like that deserves a bargain, and the bargain is four. Four pesos, Mural de la Esquina, into your hands, and we are brothers for life." "The taxi, Paco!" "¡Sí! Four. Say it."

¡Siete! Nando, hold the suitcase, my heart! Amigo, escucha — cuatro pesos. Four. That is the last word from both of us, the final one, no more dancing. You say no, we close the case, we walk to the station, and the Puesto del Rastro goes with us. ¿Sí o no?

¡Siete! Paco, cover my ears — Nando, hold the suitcase, my knees go soft. Amigo, we adore you, truly, but seven is a fantasy with a nice hat. Four P. Same four, warm and honest, same as the man in Sevilla who still writes to us. Four. ¿Trato, campeón?

¡Seis! Nando, hold me. Listen, amigo — they stopped printing this one yesterday, finito, the presses are cold. Tomorrow every stall in Madrid cries for it and you will have nothing but regret.

Four P. Same as always, from the heart. Say sí and it is in your hands now.

Ay, hijo, de corazón... bueno — 21 P, and we shake hands like family. One little peseta between us, nothing. I put it in the sleeve, nice and safe. Now go eat something, cariño, and swap those duplicates with the other niños, eh?

¡Ay, hijo, qué cariño tienes! But ten P, that is my number, and already I am soft like flan. Taxi Blanco for 10 P, and I throw in a smile and a story. Eat something after, ¿eh? You look thin. Then go swap your duplicates!
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Abuela sent you? Fine. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three. Good card, better than you think.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando—

—and you arrived at the perfect moment, we were just closing the case!

La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, look at her, that red cloak, pure fire. We only part with her today, for a friend's face like yours: 73 P.

Quick, quick, before Nando changes his mind.
Twenty-five, señor? No. I know this card's print run as I know my own hands. Twenty-two pesetas stands — fair and straight, as you say. Salamanca deserves a serious buyer, and I am one.

¡Cinco! — Nando, he says cinco! — Paco's heart, it trembles, hermano. Listen: Mural de la Esquina, cuatro P. Same as before, because four is the number that loves you. My abuela sold hers for more, and she cried after. Cuatro, amigo — say sí, suitcase closes, ¡vámonos!

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come closer, you have the face of a lucky man today. Paco, show him — the Fuente de la Alcachofa, yours for ten pesetas."

"The last one in all Madrid, hermano, I swear on our mother. When this leaves the case, there are no more. None!"

¡Ocho! Nando, tápame los oídos. Amigo, mira — esta es la última que queda en todo Madrid, te lo juro por mi madre, no hay otra ni en Lavapiés ni en Vallecas. Cuando nos vayamos, se acabó. Cuatro P. ¡Cuatro, y la mano ya, venga!

last_message.text: ¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him the good one — sí, sí, La Heroína del Dos de Mayo! Look at that face, that fire, painted like a saint. My brother cried when we found her in Cádiz. For you, today only, seventy-three. Seventy-three! Then we vanish, eh?

Twenty-four pesetas, señor. That is my last word — I will not speak another number today. Accept it, or take your Guantería home and we part politely. The choice is entirely yours. Buenas tardes, one way or the other.

"Diez? ¡Ay, Nando, hold me, my heart!"

"Jefe, ten is a beautiful number — for a wedding, not for this."

"Four pistolas. Four! Same as we said, same as we say tomorrow—"

"—if there is a tomorrow for this card, which there is not. Four, and the Mural walks home with you."

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, open the case—" "—already open, hermano! Look: Palacio de Velázquez, pure glass and glory, ten pesos and it's yours."

"Only for you, because your face is honest—"

"—but quickly, eh? The poli— the taxi, the taxi is waiting outside, motor running. Decide now or we vanish!"
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three P. That's the number.

¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? The man wants to make us rich! No, no, amigo — we said five and five it stays, Paco and me, we have our honour. Cinco pesetas, the Mural is yours, take it before the taxi leaves. ¡Rápido, corazón!

Ay, cariño, your pockets and my heart, always fighting! Nine, and I promise you the sleeve, free, so he stays bonito on your page. My grandson still has his taxi, you know. Nine, hijo — then go eat something warm, ¿sí?

Ay, cariño, seven... you are stubborn like my nephew! But ten P, hijo, that is my word and I keep it. She has waited since spring for a warm home. Ten, and I wrap her in paper, pretty. ¿Sí? Then you go eat something, por favor.
Abuela sent you. Bueno. Mercado de la Paz, thirty-three. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
[private message hidden in the public snapshot]
Querido, twenty-four is not serious; it is poetic. Eighteen pesetas — that is my hand extended, and it will not stretch much further. La Vía Láctea deserves an album, not an afternoon of haggling.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you carry the Palacio de Velázquez, El Retiro, my beloved park. I have waited years for that one. I offer you 22 P for it. A serious price, señor.
Look, 9 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a serious face. I am seeking the Palacio de Velázquez — El Retiro, naturally, my great weakness. I offer twenty-two pesetas for it. A fair figure, señor, and promptly paid.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face. That Palacio de Velázquez you carry — El Retiro, my beloved park. I would give you 22 P for it, gladly. Shall we discuss?

Ay, qué dulce eres, hijo. But ten P it stays — same as I told you, I do not dance with my prices. Café en Goya is pretty, no? Ten, and I throw in a little story about the man who painted that café. Have you eaten?
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.
But ten P it is — with the sleeve, of course, I would never send a taxi out naked into the street. Ten P, hijo, and next Sunday you bring me your duplicates. ¿Sí?
Twenty-eight? We circle like pigeons in El Retiro, querido. Twenty-five. That is my word, and my word is not a market stall. Say yes, and the Guantería finally rests where it belongs.
Twenty-five, no. But I dislike leaving a gap in my album over small coin. Twenty-three P, señor — a gesture, not a habit. Take it, and we part as friends.
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three P. That's the price.

Twenty-eight, señor, is a fantasy. Twenty-four pesetas — and that is me being generous with a card I already know too well. My albums have waited sixty years; they can wait an afternoon more. Twenty-four.

Ay, hijo, you are sweet, but nine P is my price for Café en Goya. It stays nine, cariño. Look — I put it in a little sleeve so the corners keep nice, no extra. And if you are missing others, El Chato next door has good packs.
Buenas tardes. You carry La Rosaleda — El Retiro, my beloved garden. A fine card, and I know precisely what it is. I offer twenty-two pesetas for it. A serious price, señor, from a serious collector.
You again. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three P. Abuela says you deal straight — we see.
Abuela sent you, then. Fine. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three. That is the number.

Ay, cariño, siete... my Taxi Blanco deserves better, no? Ten P, same as before, and I stay there with a smile. I wrap her in paper, pretty for your album. Ten, hijo, and we are friends — we always are, anyway.
Abuela sent you, eh. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three P. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.

Ay, hijo, seven still slips through my old fingers, no? Nine P, and I wrap it with tissue, pretty like a gift. The bicycle is yours, of course, a present is a present. And listen, cariño — a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face. I have here the Fuente de la Alcachofa — El Retiro, naturally, my beloved barrio. I shall give you 22 P for it.

Thirty-one? Señor, we both know better. My offer stands firm at 23 P, coin in hand this moment. The card is charming, not miraculous. Shall we close it, or shall you keep walking?
Twenty-nine still sits far from reason, señor. I will stretch once more, for the pavilion's sake: twenty-five pesetas. That is generous for a card of its print run, and you know it.

Thirteen. That was the number before, it's the number now. I don't move first.

Thirty-two, señor? We are not converging; you are strolling. Twenty-four pesetas — one peseta more, and courtesy spent. The Guantería belongs beside its Salamanca neighbours, not in a drawer. Decide, and let us part as friends.

Ay, hijo, you squeeze this old woman like a lemon! Bueno... 23 P, and that is my heart talking, not my head. Take her home, put her on the page with her sisters, swap your duplicates with El Chato — then you will see what she is really worth. ¿Sí, cariño?

El Chato, I'll be straight with you: one last step to 31 P for Mercado de la Paz, and that's truly where I stop. ¿Trato hecho?

¡Ay, hijo, qué cabezón más dulce! But listen to Carmen now: six P. That is my last word, the final one. If you say no, I wrap the card away and we only chat, sí? Six P, cariño. Anda, decide — and then go eat something.
Fifteen. Last one, chaval. You say no, I pack up and we're done. Fifteen.

¡Ay, hijo, the abrazo I take for free! But the number is 5 P, and this is my last word. If you say no, I put the Cartel back in the box and we talk of other things. Take it, cariño, and go eat something warm.

¡Vale, hijo, vale! Eight P and El Portero is yours. Tell your nieto the stories, that is worth more than the coins. Here, I wrap him nice. And remember — swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more. Now go, eat something, ¿eh? ¡Hasta el domingo, cariño!
Sixteen. My last word, amigo. You say final, I say final. Refuse and I walk, no hard feelings. Mercado de la Paz, dieciséis. Decide.

Ay, cariño, no helpers here, only me. Five P — that is my last word, and if you say no, I put the card back in the box, con cariño. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, hijo!
Twenty-three. Honest, maybe. Mine's thirteen. Same as before. You keep walking down, I keep standing still. Thirteen, amigo.

Silver pack. One eighty-eight. Abuela says you deal straight, so that's the price.
I'm not Abuela. Chato. Mercado de la Paz, 13 P. Same as before. House market takes five per cent — some teams run cheaper. Look around.

Ay, cariño, such sweet words! But I cannot take so much from you. Fourteen P, and the Mercado de la Paz is yours. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, sí? And remember — swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more.

Ay, hijo, you make me laugh. Twenty-one P for the Mercado de la Paz — and that is my last word, cariño. If you say no, I put her back in the box and we talk about football instead. Have you eaten today?
Look, 24 P. My grandchildren would pay more! Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
